sentence: Female patient, seen for the first time in the ophthalmology service of our hospital in 1992 (at age 33) due to decreased visual acuity in her right eye.
The initial ophthalmological examination showed a visual acuity (VA) of 0.2 in the right eye (RE) and 0.6 in the left eye (LE), with -5.0 and -4.0 spherical diopters respectively.
Biomicroscopic examination of the anterior pole revealed a marked posterior embryotoxon and intraocular pressure was 12 mmHg in both eyes.

The patient's fundus showed the following OD characteristics: Circumpapillary geographic atrophy of the RPE and choroid with precise limits that encompass the entire macular area and allow visualization of the underlying choroidal vessels.
LE: Diffuse lesions with characteristics similar to those of the RE, with a crescent of atrophy that partially affects the macular area.
In this situation, fluorescein angiography (FAG) was performed, which showed the atrophy of the RPE and choriocapillaris already described, without clear signs of activity.

Given the possibility that it was serpiginous choroiditis, immunosuppressive treatment was started with Corticosteroids and Cyclosporine, in addition to vitamin supplements due to a possible nutritional deficiency, without a favorable response being observed.
Subsequently, and due to the unfavorable evolution, immunosuppressive treatment with Azathioprine and Methotrexate was reinstated without presenting, at any time, any sign of improvement.

In 2003, and due to her family history (2 nephews genetically diagnosed with Alagille Syndrome without associated ophthalmological manifestations), a genetic study was performed on the patient, discovering the AAGT 2785+3 mutation in intron 19 of the Jagged 1 gene. and thus confirming the suspicion of Alagille Syndrome.
Currently, and after 14 years of follow-up, the patient has a visual acuity of light perception in RE and 0.1 with eccentric fixation in LE.

In the fundus, the growth of chorioretinal atrophic lesions was observed that completely covered the macular area without having shown any evidence of angiographic signs of activity in the periodic controls carried out throughout the follow-up in our service.
